evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'Sexual Healing': Gaye programmed the percussion on a Roland TR-808, drawn to it because it let him make music without other musicians or producers. Recorded at Studio Katy in Ohain, Belgium, released 9 October 1982, ten weeks at number one on the R&B chart and number three on the Hot 100.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Listen for the drum machine first: a deep, booming kick, thin clicky handclaps, a ticking snare and hissy hi-hats, all perfectly even. Nobody tried to make it sound like a drummer. Then notice that this is a slow love song by one of Motown's great singers, not an electro record from the Bronx, and that the machine works there too.

explanation: Marvin Gaye was living in Belgium, far from his old band. He used a Roland TR-808 drum machine to make 'Sexual Healing' because it let him make a whole record on his own. It was his biggest hit, in the same year that 'Planet Rock' made the 808 famous in hip-hop: the machine reached soul and electro at once, for the same reason. Its slow, sparse use here runs on to later R&B production.
